Forgotten figures

Francis Cecil Sumner, the first African American PhD in psychology

He earned his doctorate in 1920 and trained a whole generation of psychologists at Howard University.

Francis Cecil Sumner was born in Arkansas in 1895. Unable to attend high school, he studied on his own and entered university after an examination. His thesis, on the psychoanalysis of Freud and Adler, was supervised by G. Stanley Hall at Clark University, and he defended it in 1920 after returning from service in the First World War.

Training others

He was the first African American to earn a doctorate in psychology in the United States. In 1928 he joined Howard University in Washington, where he chaired the psychology department and made it a training centre for Black students at a time when many universities would not admit them.

His students included Kenneth Clark, who later carried out the doll study. Sumner also translated many German and French psychology papers into English. He died in 1954.

  1. Guthrie, R. V. (2004). Even the Rat Was White (2.ª ed.). Allyn & Bacon.
  2. Sawyer, T. F. (2000). Francis Cecil Sumner. History of Psychology, 3(2), 122–141.
